citeAs: Badertdinov, I., Golubev, A., Nekrashevich, M., Shevtsov, A., Karasik, S., Andriushchenko, A., Trofimova, M., Litvintseva, D., Yangel, B. (2025). SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents. NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track.
creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel (Nebius)
description: SWE-rebench is a public dataset of 21,336 interactive Python-based software engineering tasks mined automatically from real-world GitHub repositories. Each task is executable and verifiable, with associated environment setup information and quality metadata, and is intended for training and benchmarking software engineering agents.
name: SWE-rebench
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports validation performance for the automated quality labels. On 413 validation examples, the fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and weighted F1 0.82 for Task Complexity, 67% accuracy and weighted F1 0.65 for Test Patch Correctness, and 79% accuracy and weighted F1 0.76 for Issue Clarity.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each task instance receives automated annotations from a fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model for Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness. The model is trained on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified and predicts each binary label independently for each task.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is restricted to Python repositories where Python constitutes over 75% of the codebase and to repositories with permissive licenses, which biases coverage toward open-source Python ecosystems. The benchmark subset is additionally filtered to English problem statements, issues created in 2025, tasks with up to 3 modified files, limited patch size, and low-to-moderate LLM-assessed difficulty, further shaping the task distribution.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built through a four-stage fully automated pipeline: preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and GitHub, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and automated quality assessment. The pipeline links GitHub issues to merged pull requests, filters candidates, configures environments, executes tests in containers, and retains tasks whose tests validate the original fix.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: When git tag does not provide a version, which occurs for approximately 5% of task instances, the pipeline assigns a unique version to each remaining task so it can use its own environment. If head_commit is unavailable, the pipeline falls back to merge_commit and records this choice in metadata.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data consists of public GitHub Archive event JSON and GitHub repositories with full commit histories, including issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, pull request metadata, repository files, commits, and test/code patches.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues created before May 1, 2025 were used for the main dataset collection; the benchmark subset includes tasks whose GitHub issues were created in 2025.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that the fully automated pipeline may include imperfectly described or unsolvable tasks because quality assessment is automated rather than manually curated. The initial release is limited exclusively to Python, and automated installation and quality assessment rely on heuristics and LLM-driven judgments that may miss project subtleties or introduce errors.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After collection, pull request patches are split into solution patches and test patches. Tasks are grouped by inferred project version, candidate installation recipes are generated by an LLM with iterative refinement from logs, tests are run multiple times to exclude flaky instances, and only tasks passing execution-based verification are retained.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The pipeline merges GitHub Archive and GitHub data; links issues with pull requests mentioning resolution; filters for Python repositories with permissive licenses, resolved issues, merged PRs, single-issue links, nontrivial issue descriptions, and PRs that modify tests and non-test code; splits each PR into solution and test patches; groups tasks by normalized major.minor project versions; and records pinned dependency versions after successful setup.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper describes a continuously updated public leaderboard and states future work includes keeping the SWE-rebench benchmark up-to-date by maintaining evaluation on fresh tasks, evaluating a wider range of LLMs, and sharing detailed analyses with the community. The collection pipeline is designed for continuous supply of fresh tasks and rapid reprocessing when the pipeline changes.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors argue that the dataset can accelerate open research and improve reliable evaluation of software engineering agents, but acknowledge risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code and misuse of automated agents to introduce vulnerabilities. They frame openness, decontaminated evaluation, and rigorous benchmarking as mitigations that support responsible advancement.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking LLM-based software engineering agents, particularly for reinforcement learning on interactive tasks at scale. It is also used to construct a contamination-free benchmark and leaderboard for standardized evaluation of software engineering agents.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct is used to identify relevant repository files, extract installation recipes, iteratively refine failed recipes from logs, and provide automated task annotations. A fine-tuned Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model predicts Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness labels.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset is built from public GitHub repository and issue data, including issue descriptions, discussions, pull requests, and repository metadata from open-source projects.

null_reasons.license: paper describes source repositories having permissive licenses but does not state a license for the SWE-rebench dataset itself
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: no number of independent annotations per task is given; automated labels are described but not as repeated annotations per item
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: no human annotator demographics are provided; only model-based annotation and prior SWE-bench Verified human annotations are mentioned
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: no human annotation platform is described for SWE-rebench task labels
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: no imputation or fill-in strategy for missing feature values is described beyond assigning unique versions when version tags are absent, which is data handling rather than value imputation
